items.item: liquid clustering lets data layout evolve without rewriting existing data, improving on partitioning and ZORDER

items.item: clustering is not compatible with partitioning or ZORDER
liquid clustering is incremental: data is only rewritten as necessary; already-clustered files with different clustering columns are not rewritten

items.item: OPTIMIZE FULL is needed when clustering columns change; otherwise it behaves like OPTIMIZE
a sort order lets data be sorted within partitions by columns to gain performance, declared per data or delete file

items.item: a sort order is an id plus an ordered list of sort fields; field order determines the order the sort is applied
sort order id 0 is reserved for the unsorted order
writers are not required to use the default sort order if it is prohibitively expensive, as for streaming writes
per-file min/max statistics, null counts, and row counts are collected automatically and used at query time to skip irrelevant files

items.item: Z-ordering columns without statistics collected is ineffective and wastes compute
Databricks recommends liquid clustering for all new tables; it cannot be combined with ZORDER
clustering can stitch small files into larger ones and cluster data by sort key for query-time data locality

items.item: Hudi sorts file groups in a clustering plan by the specified columns while meeting target file sizes, by default
Hudi supports incremental scheduling, processing only partitions changed since the last completed clustering operation
Hudi's clustering service lets writers keep inserting new data while clustering runs in the background, with snapshot isolation

The 256-row dataset in examples.py is a synthetic, deliberately small and dense Cartesian product (every (a, b) pair for a, b in 0..15), not a sample of real production data, disclosed in the script's own docstring and FACT-CHECK.md red-team #1. What transfers is the real, executed mechanism — row-group bounds computed directly, and a real predicate evaluated against them.

The 'arrival order' layout is a fixed, deterministic multiplicative-hash permutation standing in for real streaming arrival order, not a claim that real arrival order always produces zero locality, per FACT-CHECK.md red-team #2.

The incremental-vs-full reclustering demonstration models Delta's own documented behavior directly, not Hudi's or Iceberg's own specific incremental-clustering implementations in detail (both are named and sourced but not separately coded), per FACT-CHECK.md red-team #4.

items.item: This topic's executed demonstration uses Z-order (bit-interleaving) specifically, not a Hilbert curve's recursive construction — both are named per the syllabus line, but Z-order is the simpler, directly-implementable mechanism; Hilbert curves achieve better locality through a different, more complex construction, named but not separately coded, per FACT-CHECK.md red-team #5.
The prerequisites panel lists topic 7 and topics 17-18, matching CHAPTER.md's own stated prerequisites-panel note for this topic.

The pruning counts (16, 4, 1 groups out of 16) are exact by construction given the chosen domain, group size, and predicate — not approximations — and the domain/group-size (16, 16) were chosen specifically so Z-order's groups align to clean 4x4 boxes in (a, b) space.

items.item: All four demonstrations in examples.py are deterministic (fixed Cartesian-product dataset, a fixed multiplicative-hash permutation, no randomness, no timing), verified byte-identical across 3 consecutive runs — no flaky-timing risk.
This topic hosts no chapter lab of its own, per CHAPTER.md's note.

The predicate used throughout (a in 4..7, b in 4..7) deliberately aligns with a single Z-order group's exact boundary, so the measured 1-group result is the best case for Z-order; a predicate straddling two quadrants would need more than one group even under Z-order, a nuance named but not separately demonstrated.
